findings.summary: The early path's new rule (refuse when origin's push URL differs from its fetch URL) has no test.
findings.evidence: The plan changes early.rs `github_repository` (early.rs:363-366), which `push_ci_branch` (:388), `delete_ci_branch` (:406) and `early_pr` (:429) all check before any push. After the change it reads origin through `origin_url`, so a split push URL makes the early push and the early pull request skip. The Risks section says a split push URL 'is refused in landing, reconcile and the early path'. But the only split-URL test is on `origin_client`. The early dependent cites `a_missing_or_non_github_origin_skips_the_early_step_silently` (run_pin_tests.rs:581-610), which covers no origin, a local path, a lookalike path and non-GitHub hosts, but not a `remote.origin.pushurl` that differs. If `github_repository` kept its old `git remote get-url origin` call, every planned test would still pass. Under the dependents rule, an entry whose test does not cover the change is a major finding. Fix: Add a split push URL case to `a_missing_or_non_github_origin_skips_the_early_step_silently`, or add a sibling test. Set origin to `https://github.com/example/project.git`, set `remote.origin.pushurl` to another path, install the early seam, call `push_ci_branch`, `early_pr` and `delete_ci_branch`, and assert the fake records no `push`, `open_pr` or `delete` calls. Name that test in the early.rs dependent entry and in the criterion 4 demonstration.
findings.location: Plan step 5 (early.rs `github_repository` via `origin_url`); Dependents entry for crates/athena-core/src/gh/early.rs; Demonstration for criterion 4

findings.summary: The end-to-end reconcile test in athena-cli quietly stops exercising the 'host refuses' path it was written for.
findings.evidence: The file header says the host is 'a fake `gh` first on PATH that refuses every call', and the lookalike origin `<tmp>/github.com/example/project.git` was chosen so `parse_remote` would build a client that asks that fake host. Under `origin_client`, the same fixture gets `NoHost`, so the fake `gh` is never called. The assertions still pass, as the plan says, but the test no longer covers a client whose host cannot name a pull request, and its doc comment becomes false. Fix: In step 5, update the header and `world()` comments of athena-cli/tests/reconcile.rs to say the lookalike origin now gets no host client (OLY-B-BND-01). Optionally, assert that the fake `gh` was never run, for example by having it write a marker file. Or name the core reconcile test that covers a host which cannot name a pull request.

findings.summary: Comparing fetch and push URLs as raw strings refuses harmless differences.
findings.evidence: `origin_url` refuses when `git remote get-url origin` and `git remote get-url --push origin` differ as strings. A push URL to the same repository written differently, such as with or without `.git`, with or without a trailing slash, or with userinfo on the push URL only, makes landing fail outright, because land_pr uses `?`. `GhClient::origin_repository` (client.rs:1026) already reduces both forms to `owner/name`. Fix: When both URLs are https github.com, compare `GhClient::origin_repository(fetch)` with `GhClient::origin_repository(push)`, and use exact string equality only otherwise. Treat multi-line `--push` output (several push URLs) as refused. Add the `.git` and no-`.git` pair to the origin_client tests as an accepted case.

findings.summary: For the no-origin case, the claim that landing does not write rests on the order of statements in land_pr, which no test checks.
findings.evidence: Criterion 4 says 'no origin (landing/push errors, no write)'. The demonstration calls only `origin_client`, plus the early seam test. It does not call `Athena::land_pr` with no origin and observe that no push and no record write happened. `land_pr` calls `athena_gate::config_at` and `landed_commit_for` around the origin lookup (landing.rs:865-894). That the `origin_client` call comes before the `GitRemote` and sink construction is only argued, not tested. Fix: Either add a land-level test where a passed job is landed with no origin (or an `upstream`-only remote), asserting Err, an unchanged `upstream` ref listing and no new records commit, or state in the demonstration that ordering is checked by reading landing.rs.

summary: I checked the plan against the snapshot with Read and Grep; I ran nothing. The plan targets the right places. All production pushes go through the remote.rs `GitRemote` push, replace and delete_branch methods (remote.rs:52-79), athena-git `push_branch` and `push_if_remote_at` (lib.rs:384-434), and `append_to_remote` (records_branch.rs:401-444). Every existing caller and test passes "origin"; the one exception, gh/tests.rs:4004 with "elsewhere", still expects an error containing that name, which the new text includes. `Options::with_remote` has no callers. The pull-request target comes from origin. `origin_client` reuses the strict `GhClient::origin_repository` (client.rs:1026) and closes the lookalike-path hole in `parse_remote`. `hestia::parse_spec`, `measure_problem` and `spec_gaps` exist, and a measure ending `status: not shown` passes `measure_problem`. Keeping CHANGELOG.md untouched matches criterion 7, and the conflict is raised as a question. No landing-classification function changes, so no commit-shape table is needed. The one major gap: the early path's new split-push-URL refusal has no test. The existing early-origin test does not cover it, so a missed early.rs edit would go unseen. Minor points: the athena-cli reconcile test silently stops reaching its fake host and its header comment becomes false; raw string comparison of the fetch and push URLs refuses harmless differences such as a `.git` suffix; and that landing does not write when there is no origin is argued from statement order, not tested. Athena's own findings about files outside the deliverables list are not repeated.
